steps.title: Import React and ReactNode from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and ReactNode from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in both React and ReactNode from 'react'.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and ReactNode. This gives you access to React for creating components and ReactNode for typing children props.

steps.title: Create a Card component with typed props
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Card that accepts props with a children property typed as ReactNode. The component should return an empty div element for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named Card that takes a props parameter with a typed children property.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { ReactNode } from 'react';

// Create your Card component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component function is created with proper TypeScript typing for the children prop.
successCriteria:
The code should include a Card component function that:
1. Is named 'Card'
2. Accepts a props parameter with a children property typed as ReactNode
3. Returns a JSX element (empty div for now)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a Card component with proper TypeScript typing for the children prop. This is the foundation for accepting and rendering child content.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You're on the right track, but there are a few issues. Make sure your Card component:
1. Has the correct name 'Card'
2. Accepts props with a children property typed as ReactNode
3. Returns a JSX element (like an empty div)
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component wasn't created correctly. You need to define a function named Card that takes props with a children property typed as ReactNode and returns a JSX element.

steps.title: Define Card component props interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named CardProps for your Card component's props. The interface should include a children property with the type ReactNode.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by CardProps, then define children: ReactNode inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CardProps interface with a children property typed as ReactNode, ready to be used in the Card component.
successCriteria: The interface must be named CardProps and include a children property of type ReactNode.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the CardProps interface with the children property typed as ReactNode. This provides type safety for the component's children.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface is named CardProps and includes a children property with the correct type ReactNode.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to create an interface named CardProps with a children property of type ReactNode.

steps.title: Implement Card component structure
steps.instruction: Create the Card component function that returns a div wrapper element. The component should accept props of type CardProps and return JSX.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named Card that takes props as a parameter and returns a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component is defined as a function that returns a div element and accepts CardProps as its parameter.
successCriteria: The code should contain a Card component definition (function or arrow function) that returns a div element and has props typed as CardProps.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Card component structure. The component now accepts props and returns a div wrapper, which will be the foundation for rendering children content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Card component: 1) Is defined as a function or arrow function, 2) Accepts props typed as CardProps, and 3) Returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a component function that accepts CardProps and returns a div element.

steps.title: Render children prop inside Card
steps.instruction: Inside your Card component's return statement, render the children prop that was defined in the CardProps interface.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces {} to render the children prop value inside your component's structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will now display any content passed between its opening and closing tags.
successCriteria: The children prop is rendered inside the Card component's return statement using JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully rendered the children prop inside your Card component. This allows the Card to display any content passed to it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering the children prop inside the Card component's return statement using JSX curly braces {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The children prop needs to be rendered inside the Card component. Look for where you should display the content passed to the Card.

steps.title: Create a Button component with typed props
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named Button that accepts typed props including children. Define it after the Card component.
steps.hint: You can use either function Button() or const Button = () => {}. Make sure to include a props parameter with proper typing.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Button component is created with proper TypeScript typing for its props, ready to accept children.
successCriteria: The Button component should be defined as a function (either function declaration or arrow function) with a typed props parameter that includes a children prop. It should return JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Button component with proper TypeScript typing. This component is now ready to accept children content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few issues. Make sure the Button component is properly defined with typed props that include children, and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component isn't properly defined. You need to create a functional component named Button with typed props that include children.

steps.title: Implement Button component with children
steps.instruction: Implement the Button component to return a button element that renders children. The component should accept children as a prop and render them inside a button element.
steps.hint: Create a button element that displays the children prop inside it. Remember to use the ButtonProps interface you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component is implemented and returns a button element that renders the children prop.
successCriteria: Button component is implemented
Component returns a button element
Button element renders children prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the Button component to render children inside a button element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Button component returns a button element that renders the children prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component implementation is missing or incorrect. It should return a button element that renders the children prop.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX.
steps.hint: Define a component function called App that returns a JSX element. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component function that returns JSX.
successCriteria: The code includes a component named App that returns a JSX element (e.g., a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a component named App that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined. Ensure you create a component named App that returns JSX.
